title: The scan cycle: why the order of the rungs matters
summary: Learn that a PLC reads its inputs, solves the rungs from top to bottom and then writes its outputs, and fix a program whose lamp follows the button one scan too late.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety, and it does not measure how long a scan takes on a real controller.
objectives: Describe the scan cycle: read the inputs, solve the rungs from top to bottom, write the outputs, and repeat.
Find why an output lags one scan behind its input, fix it without changing a contact or a coil, and see the difference of one scan in the recorded trace.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/ScanOrder.ld.json two rungs are drawn. One copies the button StartButton into a memory bit ButtonSeen, and the other shows ButtonSeen on the Lamp. The lamp follows the button one scan late. Make the lamp follow the button in the same scan.
stages.checkpoint: You can say which of the two rungs calculates a value and which one uses it.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, predict Lamp. The scenario presses the button at {{t:10}} ms and releases it at {{t:30}} ms. With the rungs in the right order, when does the lamp light, and when does it go out?
stages.checkpoint: {{v:ScanOrder.Lamp=true@10|Lamp ON}} at {{t:10}} ms, in the same scan as the press; {{v:ScanOrder.Lamp=false@30|lamp OFF}} at {{t:30}} ms, in the same scan as the release.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct the starting program, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}. The starting program lights the lamp one scan late, at {{t:20}} ms instead of {{t:10}} ms. Change it so that Lamp turns ON at {{t:10}} ms and OFF at {{t:30}} ms, in the same scans as StartButton. Keep every contact and coil as it is.
stages.checkpoint: {{ui:learn.check}} reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press {{ui:learn.check}}. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson and lists every assertion that failed.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named ScanOrder and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Compare {{t:10}}, {{t:20}} and {{t:30}} ms in the trace: the lamp changes in the same row as the button. With the wrong order the lamp row would change one row later.
stages.checkpoint: Lamp rises once at {{t:10}} ms and falls once at {{t:30}} ms, in the same scan as the button.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: A scan takes the same few milliseconds every time. Why can a one-scan delay be harmless in one machine and a problem in another? What would happen if the lamp were a fast counter input?
stages.checkpoint: A delay of one scan only matters when something needs the value sooner: a chain of rungs adds a scan per link, and a pulse shorter than a scan can come and go unseen.

hints.text: Look at which rung writes ButtonSeen and which rung reads it, and where each of them sits in the program.
Select the rung that copies StartButton into ButtonSeen and press {{ui:ld.moveRungUp}} once, so that it becomes rung 1. Do not change any contact or coil.

faultCases: The starting program lights the lamp one scan late, at {{t:20}} ms instead of {{t:10}} ms.
